A complete analyzer first reads data, then computes characteristics, then prints a consistently formatted report. Do not change the original order for one characteristic if another needs it. Use map for frequencies, a sorted copy for the median, and a wide accumulator for the sum.

Empty-input and tie conventions are part of the project. If the median is defined only for a nonempty odd-sized collection, explicitly restrict the input. texts.cpp.arrays.theory:
An array stores a sequence of elements of the same type. For three integers, you can write int data[3] = {4, 7, 2};. The indices are 0, 1 and 2. In modern code, std::array<int, 3> data = {4, 7, 2}; from <array> is convenient for a fixed size. It provides size(), access with [] and range-based for iteration.

[] does not check bounds: an ordinary element's index must be strictly less than the size. data.at(index) checks the bound and throws std::out_of_range if it is violated; exception handling comes later, and these tasks guarantee valid indices. To read three values into an array, use an index-based loop. Changing a copy in range for does not change the array element; use data[i] for writing.

In standard C++, a built-in array's size must be a valid constant expression, not an arbitrary n read from cin. For an input-dependent size, use vector.

int energy = 20; creates an object with an initial value. energy = 12; changes an existing object. Assignment evaluates the right-hand side first, then stores the result on the left: energy = energy + 5; adds 5 to the previous value. It is not a mathematical equality.

The shorthand energy += 5; does the same for our integer variable. The operators -= and *= work similarly. After assignment, the old value is lost unless you saved it elsewhere. To exchange values, use a temporary variable: int saved = a; a = b; b = saved;. Names must start with a letter or underscore; for these exercises, choose clear Latin-letter names and avoid reserved naming patterns.

texts.cpp.binarylab.theory:
In a sorted array, find the first index whose value is ≥x. Maintain the half-open candidate range [low,high), initially [0,n). While low<high, let mid=low+(high-low)/2. If a[mid]<x, the boundary is strictly to the right: low=mid+1; otherwise high=mid. At termination, low is the answer, sometimes n. Index n denotes an insertion position, not permission to read a[n]. The search area strictly decreases.

std::lower_bound returns the first element ≥x; std::upper_bound returns the first >x. Both require appropriate range ordering. For vector, comparisons take O(log n); the distance between upper_bound and lower_bound is the count of x. For a value interval [lo,hi], use upper_bound(hi)-lower_bound(lo), but handle lo>hi first.

Binary search also applies to an answer. To ship positive weights in their original order within a day limit named days, a capacity-C check greedily fills the current day, starting another when C would be exceeded. If shipping is possible at C, it is possible at every larger capacity. The lower bound is the maximum weight; the upper bound is the sum. Empty cargo gives 0. Complexity is O(n log S), where S is the sum of weights; a correct monotone predicate check is required, not just a familiar loop.

An if / else if / else chain checks conditions from top to bottom and executes only the first matching branch. Unlike independent if statements, it prevents repeated output. Start with conditions that must not be hidden by broader ones.

switch (code) selects a case label using an integer or character value. break exits the switch; without it, execution may continue into the following case. default handles other values. Use if for ranges and compound logic, and switch for individual codes. Here, break exits switch; its role in loops will be studied separately.

texts.cpp.capstone.theory:
The final project is a small console dispatcher. Items have names, commands change quantities, and a failed withdrawal preserves the previous state. Use map for lookup by name and a class for an individual invariant if it improves clarity. No complicated UI or unjustified dependencies are needed.

Readiness criteria: the program compiles as C++17/20; every response follows the protocol; an empty catalog is valid; repeated deliveries accumulate; insufficient stock does not reduce the remainder; querying a missing item does not accidentally create it. Test command sequences, not just a single state.

After solving it, explain aloud: where data is stored, which objects own resources, when references become invalid, which code handles input, and where success is confirmed. These questions connect practice with university theory.

texts.cpp.characters.theory:
The loop for (char ch : text) iterates over a string's elements by value. The variable ch is a copy of the current char; changing ch does not change text. To build a result, create an empty std::string result and append suitable characters using result += ch;. This is a range-based for loop: it traverses an existing sequence without a manual index.

In this lesson, input is restricted to ASCII: Latin letters, digits and spaces. Test for a digit using '0' <= ch && ch <= '9'. The standard guarantees consecutive codes for decimal digits; ch - '0' gives a digit's numeric value. Do not generalize letter ranges to every encoding and language. A direct comparison ch == 'a' checks for that specific character.

texts.cpp.complexity.theory:
O(n) describes an asymptotic upper bound on how costs grow, not an exact time in seconds. One pass usually makes a number of checks proportional to n. Two consecutive passes are still O(n); two fully nested passes are O(n²). std::sort requires O(n log n) comparisons in this model.

std::binary_search(v.begin(),v.end(),target) checks for a value in a sorted range and returns bool. For vector, the number of comparisons is logarithmic. Sorting for a single search usually costs more preparation than a linear search. With many searches, ordering may pay off. Algorithm preconditions are mandatory: do not use binary_search on arbitrary unordered input.

A console menu can work without graphical buttons: the program reads commands and updates state. A protocol specifies exact words, arguments and response formats. In this project, ADD x adds a number, TOTAL prints the sum, and STOP ends execution. Reading std::string command in while(cin>>command) also stops at the end of input.

Decide separately what is stored, what each command changes, and which message is printed. Do not add greetings unless the protocol requests them. Use functions for computation and main for interaction. For an unrecognized command, the project prints Invalid and stops rather than guessing the user's intention.

For each scenario, check an empty log, several commands, and termination without extra output.

const int limit=10; prevents modifying limit after initialization. const does not mean a value must be known at compile time: const int value=read(); may obtain its result at runtime. constexpr int limit=10; requires a constant expression for that variable.

A constexpr function may participate in compile-time evaluation if the call meets the requirements, but it may also be called with ordinary runtime input. static_assert(condition, "message"); checks a constant condition at compile time.

A constructor has the type's name and no return type: Meter(int start) : value_(start) {}. The list after the colon initializes fields before the constructor body runs. This is not an ordinary method call after creation. Fields are initialized in their declaration order in the class, not the list's order.

An operation's result type is determined by its operands, not by the destination variable. double x = 5 / 2; stores 2.0 because integer division has already happened. texts.cpp.division.theory:
When both operands are integers, / performs integer division: 17 / 5 gives 3. The remainder operator % complements that division: 17 % 5 gives 2. For nonnegative a and positive b, a = (a / b) * b + a % b, and the remainder is between 0 and b-1.

For negative integers, the quotient is truncated towards zero: -17 / 5 is -3, and -17 % 5 is -2. This is not rounding down. Our packaging tasks use nonnegative numbers, so the everyday interpretation of a remainder applies. Neither / nor % may use a zero divisor. When a divisor is read, the task guarantees that it is positive.

texts.cpp.dynamic.summary: Separate an object's lifetime from the pointer's local name.
texts.cpp.dynamic.theory:
new int(value) creates an int in dynamic memory and returns a pointer. delete p ends that object's lifetime and releases its allocated memory. After delete, you must not read *p. The pointer itself does not automatically become null; p=nullptr may make later accidental use easier to spot, but does not fix other copies of the same address.

Losing the only way to reach an allocated object without releasing it causes a leak. Deleting the same object twice is invalid. Array new[] requires delete[], not ordinary delete. This lesson uses only a single int and one new/delete pair. It explains the mechanism, not a recommendation to manage memory manually in an ordinary app. The next lesson replaces the manual pair with an RAII owner.

For a one-shot task, you can finish with Invalid. Interactive retry requires clearing failbit with clear() and discarding the invalid remainder; do not loop forever on the same token.

vector.at(index) throws std::out_of_range for an invalid index. A try { ... } catch(const std::out_of_range&) { ... } block handles that specific error; include <stdexcept>. A // comment continues to the end of the source line and is not executed. A /* ... */ comment can span several lines. Inside quotation marks, // is just text. Do not hide the only required statements inside a comment.

std::ifstream input("data.txt") from <fstream> opens a file for reading relative to the process's working directory. if(!input) checks whether opening succeeded. Reading input>>value resembles cin, while while(input>>value) reads numbers until a failure. That loop alone does not distinguish end of file from a malformed token; further checks come later.

std::ofstream output("journal.txt") creates or truncates a file by default. Use std::ios::app to append. Check opening before writing and the state afterwards; when needed, output.close() followed by another check detects deferred errors. The stream closes its resource through RAII.

texts.cpp.first.theory:
An algorithm is a finite sequence of steps that an executor can follow. A program expresses an algorithm in a programming language. C++ is case-sensitive: main and Main are different names.

An ordinary console program starts executing in int main(). Braces enclose its body. The statement std::cout << "Ready"; sends text to standard output. A semicolon ends the statement; quotation marks delimit the text and are not printed. The directive #include <iostream> makes input/output declarations available. For now, use this structure without trying to memorize every detail.

In codelib, you can write code, save it and compare it with a reference solution. There is no built-in execution yet. Do not confuse marking a task complete yourself with checking a program using a compiler.

texts.cpp.flow.theory:
break exits the nearest loop or switch. continue skips the remainder of the current iteration: in for, the step executes next, followed by the condition; in while, the condition is checked immediately. A misplaced continue can skip a while counter update and create an infinite loop.

In nested loops, the inner loop runs through its iterations for each outer value. For a table of rows lines and cols characters, the outer loop handles lines and the inner loop handles each line's contents. Print the newline after the inner loop.

When streaming a known number of values, do not stop reading early without a reason: if more data is needed afterwards, the unread values remain in the input stream.

texts.cpp.for.summary: Repeat an action a known number of times.
texts.cpp.for.theory:
for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) { ... } creates a counter i, tests the condition before each iteration, and increments i after the body. With n=3, the body sees i equal to 0, 1 and 2. ++i increments the variable by one. For now, use increment as a separate step rather than inside complex expressions.

If the condition is false initially, the body executes zero times. A variable declared in the for header is available inside the loop, but not after it. To accumulate a sum, create sum=0 before the loop and add values inside. Do not reset sum on every iteration.

Plan output separators separately: if (i > 0) before a space can avoid a trailing space.

texts.cpp.functions.theory:
A function groups statements under a name. int square(int value) { return value * value; } takes one int and returns an int. The call square(4) evaluates the argument 4, passes it to the parameter value and obtains the result 16. A parameter is a name inside the function; an argument is a value at the call site.

return ends the current function and passes its result to the caller. A returned value is not printed by itself: you must store or print it. Functions that return an ordinary value must return it on every execution path. void denotes a function with no return value.

In this lesson, declare functions before main so their names are already known at each call. Do not try to define one ordinary function inside another.

texts.cpp.getline.theory:
std::getline(std::cin, line) reads text up to the end of a line, preserves spaces within it, and removes the terminating newline delimiter from the result. An empty input line produces an empty std::string. If you read a number with >> before getline, the newline at the end of its line normally remains in the input stream. The first getline may then read just that empty remainder.

When the format says 'a number on a separate line, then text', you can discard the rest of the number's line: std::cin.ignore(std::numeric_limits<std::streamsize>::max(), '\n');. Include <limits> for this. It deliberately removes everything up to the end of the first line. Do not apply it blindly when useful text is on the same line.

std::ws before getline discards all leading whitespace and empty lines; it is not a universal replacement when they matter.

texts.cpp.invalidation.theory:
vector may reallocate memory as it grows. If push_back causes reallocation, previous pointers, references and iterators to its elements are invalidated. Without reallocation, push_back preserves references to existing elements, but the previous end changes. Thus, 'it always breaks everything' is inaccurate too.

A simple safe strategy is to save an index, append, then obtain the element again using that index, if it still denotes the intended record. reserve sets capacity without creating elements; resize changes size and creates or removes elements. Erasing may shift records, so an index alone is not a universal stable ID. This app associates learning progress with stable IDs, not array positions.

An iterator denotes a position in a sequence. values.begin() points to the beginning; values.end() denotes the position past the last element. Algorithms usually take a half-open range [begin,end): the beginning is included, and the end is excluded. An empty range has begin==end. You must not dereference end.

<algorithm> provides std::count(values.begin(), values.end(), target), which counts matches. std::find returns an iterator to the first match, or the supplied end if there are no matches. Compare the iterator with end before reading the element using *it. Here, auto preserves the iterator's exact type. You do not need to move iterators manually yet.

Reliable file handling begins with input validation. If input contains an error, you must not destroy the old log first and then report Invalid. Read and validate the data in memory before opening the file for writing. This is not yet fully atomic persistence: failure during overwriting remains dangerous. Real persistence uses a temporary file on the same filesystem, checks, and atomic replacement through OS facilities. This standard C++ exercise demonstrates only validation before modification.

Examples show initial and expected file contents. Reading, computation and writing are separate stages. Do not call a file saved until writing and closing have completed successfully.

texts.cpp.lifetime.theory:
An ordinary local object exists until execution leaves its block. Keeping a pointer or reference longer does not make that object live forever. You must not return an int* to a function's local int and then read through it in the caller. Return an int by value: the returned value provides an independent result.

The 'stack' is a useful implementation model for local calls, but the standard describes storage duration and lifetime without requiring one specific hardware structure. Dynamic memory can outlive a call; managing it is introduced separately.

For an array, a pointer may move only within its permitted array range and the one-past-the-end position. A one-past-the-end pointer is valid for comparison and traversal, not for reading an element.

texts.cpp.logic.theory:
&& means logical AND: both conditions must hold. || means OR: at least one must hold. ! changes true to false and vice versa. To check whether x belongs to [a,b], write a <= x && x <= b. The spelling a <= x <= b does not mean a range: it chains two separate comparisons with an intermediate bool.

&& and || short-circuit: the right-hand side of && is evaluated only when the left-hand side is true, and the right-hand side of || only when the left-hand side is false. This allows divisor != 0 && value % divisor == 0 to avoid division by zero. Parentheses around meaningful groups improve readability; ! has higher precedence than &&, which has higher precedence than ||.

texts.cpp.maps.theory:
std::map<std::string,int> from <map> associates a unique key with a number. counts[word] returns the value for a key and, if the key is absent, inserts it with an initial int value of 0. This makes ++counts[word] convenient for counting frequencies. But even reading through [] can modify a map; to check presence without insertion, use find and compare with end.

The loop for(const auto& entry : counts) reads pairs: entry.first is the key, and entry.second is the value. By default, map iterates over keys in comparison order — lexicographically for our words of Latin letters. size() counts distinct keys, not the total number of additions. map alone does not preserve the arrival order of messages.

texts.cpp.methods.theory:
A method is a function called on an object: counter.add();. Inside a method, that object's fields are accessible by name. The method int value() const promises not to modify the object's ordinary state through this and can be called on a const object. For our simple classes, this is an enforceable read-only restriction.

In class, fields and methods are private by default. A public: section exposes the interface. Private fields cannot be read directly from main; access goes through methods. This is not secrecy against an attacker, but a language boundary that preserves state rules. Initial field values protect against accidental uninitialized state.

texts.cpp.pointerslab.recap: Check empty arrays, one element, duplicates, equal values at different positions, and the remainder during merging.
texts.cpp.pointerslab.summary: Use order and an invariant for a linear pass.
texts.cpp.pointerslab.theory:
In a sorted array, find a pair of distinct indices with a given sum. Start with left=0, right=n-1. If the sum is too small, increase left: the current left element with any smaller right element is too small too. If too large, decrease right for the symmetric reason. Stop at left≥right: one element cannot pair with itself. Here, 'pointer' means an index, not a raw C++ address.

Merging two sorted arrays takes the smaller current element until one array ends, then appends the other's remainder. For intersection, matching elements enter the result, and duplicates can be skipped. Sorted input is mandatory: arbitrary input breaks the proof.

If a[left]+a[right]≤limit, every pair of current left with indices left+1 through right qualifies: there are right-left of them. This counts pairs of indices, not distinct value pairs. Another two-boundary technique is a duplicate-free window: map stores frequencies, and the left edge moves until the duplicate disappears. It also works with negative values because the restriction concerns repetition, not a sum.
texts.cpp.pointerslab.title: Two pointers without losing candidates

texts.cpp.prefixlab.balance.hint.2: The right sum starts after i: p[n]-p[i+1].

texts.cpp.prefixlab.even.hint.1: Sum indicators, not the values themselves.
texts.cpp.prefixlab.even.hint.2: x%2==0 also works for negative even numbers.

texts.cpp.prefixlab.meaning.explanation: r can equal n, and the range can be empty; p[r]-p[l] covers both cases.
texts.cpp.prefixlab.meaning.hint.1: p[r] includes elements with indices below r.

texts.cpp.prefixlab.meaning.title: What does a prefix store?
texts.cpp.prefixlab.microscope: The identity p[i+1]-p[i]=a[i] explains subtraction: the shared prefix cancels. It does not assume positivity. Difference arrays use a different invariant: the accumulated adjustment at i equals the sum of all updates covering i. An empty [l,l) changes nothing.
texts.cpp.prefixlab.queries.explanation: Empty ranges automatically yield zero; total complexity is O(n+q).
texts.cpp.prefixlab.queries.hint.1: Build prefixes once before all queries.
texts.cpp.prefixlab.queries.hint.2: The right index already addresses p: use p[r]-p[l].
texts.cpp.prefixlab.queries.prompt: First, n (0–1000) and n integer elements (−1000000–1000000). Then q (0–1000) and q pairs l r (0≤l≤r≤n). Print the sum of each [l,r) on its own line.
texts.cpp.prefixlab.queries.title: Range-sum queries
texts.cpp.prefixlab.recap: State what p[i] means; check an empty range, the whole array and the final bound n. Do not confuse inclusive and exclusive right endpoints.
texts.cpp.prefixlab.summary: Move from one pass to many queries without repeated summation.
texts.cpp.prefixlab.theory:
The half-open range [l,r) includes l but excludes r; its length is r-l. For an n-element array, bounds 0≤l≤r≤n are allowed, including an empty range. Create p of size n+1: p[0]=0, p[i+1]=p[i]+a[i]. Then p[i] stores the sum of the first i elements, and the sum of [l,r) is p[r]-p[l]. Construction takes O(n), each query O(1), and memory O(n). Negative elements do not affect the formula.

Count properties in the same way: instead of a[i], add 1 for an even element and 0 otherwise. For an equilibrium index i, the left sum is p[i] and the right sum is p[n]-p[i+1]; the element itself belongs to neither side.

The reverse idea is a difference array: mark adding d to [l,r) with diff[l]+=d, diff[r]-=d, then accumulate adjustments from left to right. Marking r=n needs size n+1. Here, arrays have at most 1000 elements, values and adjustments are at most a million in magnitude, and there are at most 1000 updates. long long comfortably covers these sums; arbitrary signed overflow remains invalid.
texts.cpp.prefixlab.title: Prefix sums and half-open ranges

texts.cpp.priority.theory:
Multiplication * and division / have higher precedence than + and -. Parentheses change the grouping: (a + b) * c adds a and b first. Operators + and - at the same precedence level group from left to right: a - b - c means (a - b) - c.

Unary minus changes a value's sign: -x. Use named intermediate results to keep expressions readable. Do not rely on notation such as 2(a+b): C++ requires explicit multiplication, as in 2 * (a + b).

In this lesson, every intermediate integer result is between −30000 and 30000. This avoids overflow even on an implementation with the minimum required int range.
texts.cpp.priority.title: Expression grouping

texts.cpp.raii.microscope: RAII does not mean 'the program cannot crash and will never lose anything'. For example, immediate process termination or a system failure can bypass ordinary object destruction. Under normal control flow, an automatic owner greatly reduces the paths that lead to leaks.
texts.cpp.raii.owned.explanation: The owner type carries responsibility for release.
texts.cpp.raii.owned.hint.2: unique_ptr releases the object when main exits.

texts.cpp.raii.reset.explanation: An owner can release its resource before its block ends.
texts.cpp.raii.reset.hint.2: After reset, you may compare p with nullptr but must not read *p.
texts.cpp.raii.reset.prompt: Input: n (−100–100). Create a unique_ptr<int>, copy its value into saved, call reset(), then print saved and the result of p==nullptr.
texts.cpp.raii.reset.title: End a resource explicitly
texts.cpp.raii.summary: Let an owner object manage the resource.
texts.cpp.raii.theory:
RAII ties a resource to an owner object's lifetime. std::unique_ptr<int> from <memory> owns a single int and releases it when the owner is destroyed, including normal block exit and stack unwinding due to an exception. auto p=std::make_unique<int>(7); creates an owner without explicit new. Access the value with *p. Manually deleting an object owned by unique_ptr is unnecessary and dangerous.

unique_ptr ownership cannot be copied. auto q=std::move(p); transfers it to another unique_ptr; include <utility>. In this particular move, p becomes empty and q owns the original object. std::move itself is a cast; the type's move operation performs the actual transfer. reset() releases the managed object and leaves the owner empty.
texts.cpp.raii.title: unique_ptr and automatic release
texts.cpp.raii.transfer.explanation: For unique_ptr, this transfer leaves the source empty; do not generalize that state to every type after std::move.

texts.cpp.raii.transfer.hint.2: Use std::move(p), then read only through q.

texts.cpp.references.recap: int gives a copy; int& gives access to the original object; const T& allows reading without a copy through that reference.

texts.cpp.references.theory:
int& alias = value; creates a reference: another name for an existing int. It must be initialized; assigning alias=7 changes value itself. You cannot later 'rebind' the reference: alias=other copies other's value into the bound object.

An int& parameter lets a function work with the original variable: void add(int& value,int bonus). The call requires a suitable object, not an arbitrary temporary expression. const std::vector<int>& provides access without copying and without permission to modify elements through that reference. const restricts modification through that access path.

In a range for, for (int& value : values) lets you modify elements in place. Distinguish & in a reference declaration from the address-of operation in the next lesson.

texts.cpp.representations.theory:
Unsigned arithmetic is performed modulo 2^N for the corresponding type: decrementing zero unsigned by 1 gives its maximum value. This is a defined rule, not signed overflow. However, mixing signed and unsigned can unexpectedly convert a negative number to a large unsigned value.

std::numeric_limits<T>::max() from <limits> gives the type's maximum value; for integers, digits gives the number of value bits, excluding the sign. Do not assume int is exactly 32 bits in portable explanations. For a wider product, convert an operand before multiplication: 1LL*a*b. The LL suffix denotes long long.

Converting double to an integer requires the truncated result to be representable; do not try it on an arbitrarily huge number.

texts.cpp.scope.microscope: Scope is a property of a name in the source text; lifetime is the period during execution when an object exists. They are related but different concepts. For simple local ints, both end at the block boundary, but do not generalize this to all objects and kinds of storage.

texts.cpp.scope.theory:
A local variable's name is available from its declaration to the end of its block. Separate calls to a function have their own parameters and local objects. The function void bump(int value) { ++value; } changes only a copy of the int; the original variable stays unchanged. To change a result without references, return the new value and assign it explicitly: count = bumped(count);.

The declaration int bumped(int value); tells the compiler the name, return type and parameters. You can place the definition with its body after main. The prototype must match the definition; it does not contain an implementation by itself. A local object's lifetime usually ends when execution leaves the block. Do not use its name outside its scope.
texts.cpp.scope.title: Scope and copies

texts.cpp.searchtext.theory:
text.find('-') returns the position of the first hyphen, or the special value std::string::npos if there is none. Positions start at 0. A convenient way to store the result is auto position = text.find('-');: auto deduces the type from the initializer; it does not make the type dynamic. Do not store npos in int or test position<0.

text.substr(start, count) creates a substring beginning at start, with at most count elements. text.substr(start) takes the remainder of the string. start must not exceed size(); when start==size(), the result is empty. Indexing text[index] reads the element at that position; ordinary elements require index<size(). In these tasks, use find and substr, checking that the separator exists before calculating position+1.

std::string::npos is a 'not found' marker, not a valid character position.

texts.cpp.searchvector.theory:
Linear search checks elements one by one. To find the first position, keep index=-1 when nothing has been found, then store i at the first match. In this model, real positions run from 0 to n-1, so −1 cannot be confused with one. After the search, do not use values[index] until you have checked index!=-1.

To change every element, use an index-based loop: values[i] += bonus;. A range for with int value would change only a copy. Equal values may occur many times: decide in advance whether you need the first match, the last, or all matches.

Do not add or remove container elements during an ordinary range for over that container: structural changes may invalidate the traversal. Here, filter into a separate result or change only existing elements' values.

texts.cpp.sorting.theory:
std::sort from <algorithm> sorts vector elements in ascending order: std::sort(v.begin(), v.end());. Equal elements remain, but sort does not promise to preserve their relative order. For numbers with no additional fields, this distinction is usually invisible. Empty and single-element ranges are valid.

After sorting, the minimum is at the beginning and the maximum at the end, but reading v[0] or v[n-1] is valid only when n>0. Sorting changes the original order; if you need it later, make a copy first. For descending order, you can sort in ascending order and then apply reverse; another option is a comparator, introduced after the basic model.

For text, include <string> and create std::string name;. Input using std::cin >> name reads one word up to a whitespace separator; leading whitespace is skipped. Print a string using std::cout << name;. The + operator joins strings: name + "!" creates new text, while += appends to the existing string. You cannot apply + directly to two string literals: at least one operand must be a std::string.

name.size() returns the number of char elements, and name.empty() checks for emptiness. Strings can be compared using == and !=. In this lesson, input words consist of Latin letters. For UTF-8, size() counts bytes, not necessarily visible characters. A string is an object in its own right; copying a std::string creates an independent value.

Point p{3,4}; initializes the aggregate's fields in declaration order. Each object has its own fields; Point q=p copies their values.

A structure is useful instead of parallel arrays: an item's name, quantity and price belong to one record. std::vector<Point> stores several points just as vector<int> stored numbers. Passing const Point& lets you read fields without copying and without modification through that reference.

texts.cpp.telemetry.theory:
You do not need to store every sequence in full. A sum needs an accumulator, a maximum needs the best value so far, and a count of rises needs the preceding measurement. These are streaming algorithms: read a new value, update the state, and move on.

Initialize the maximum of a nonempty sequence from its first value, not from zero: when every number is negative, zero is not their maximum. Compare adjacent measurements starting with the second one. The n≥1 contract makes it safe to read the first element separately.

The final task uses long long for the sum and floating-point division for the average.

A test is a specific input with an expected result. Choose boundaries, empty cases, equality, negative values and cases that distinguish similar algorithms. For a maximum function, {-8,-3,-12} exposes incorrect initialization to zero; {1,2,3} does not.

assert(condition) from <cassert> terminates a checking program when the condition is false, unless assertions are disabled by NDEBUG. It is a development tool, not release-mode handling of invalid user input. Guaranteed product checks require explicit branches and results.

Compare two independent algorithms on small inputs: a streaming sum and a sum after storage should match. A random test does not prove correctness in general, and the compiler does not check the meaning of an expected answer.

texts.cpp.translation.summary: Distinguish declarations, definitions and build stages.
texts.cpp.translation.theory:
The preprocessor handles directives such as #include; a header normally provides declarations and definitions that the compiler must see. Compiling each translation unit produces object code; linking connects definitions into a program. A function declaration states its interface, while its definition contains the body.

If an ordinary declared function is called but the program lacks its required definition, a typical diagnostic appears during linking. A syntax error is usually caught earlier. Not every error requires a diagnostic: runtime undefined behavior may produce no warning.

The external command clang++ -std=c++17 main.cpp -o app compiles and links; ./app runs the program. Several source files can be supplied in one command. These are developer commands, not a built-in codelib feature. For library names, std:: is namespace qualification; #include does not mean using namespace std.

double stores numbers with a fractional part: double distance = 2.5;. In C++ source, use a dot as the decimal separator. int stores integers; converting double to int discards the fractional part towards zero, provided that the result is representable.

char marker = 'A'; stores one character code unit written in single quotation marks; "A" is a string literal, not a char. A Russian character usually occupies several bytes in UTF-8, so one char cannot be promised to hold any letter. bool ready = true; stores true or false. Without special formatting, printing a bool produces 1 or 0.

For a fixed number of decimal places, include <iomanip> and output std::fixed << std::setprecision(2). This changes stream formatting, not the stored number. Valid numeric input in these tasks uses a decimal dot.

texts.cpp.undefined.theory:
Undefined behavior means the standard imposes no requirements on an execution that reaches such a violation. It need not produce an exception, a hang or zero. C++17/20 examples include signed overflow, integer division by zero, reading through a dangling pointer and accessing outside the valid elements. Do not ask for such a program's exact output as an unambiguous test.

Distinguish implementation-defined behavior, where an implementation chooses and documents a variant (such as certain type characteristics), from unspecified behavior, where several permitted variants exist without a requirement to document the particular choice. Not every unfamiliar program has undefined behavior: unsigned modular arithmetic and -17/5 are defined.

Defensive code checks preconditions before a dangerous operation. Compiler checks and sanitizers help, but the absence of a warning does not prove the absence of undefined behavior.

texts.cpp.vector.theory:
std::vector<int> values(n); from <vector> creates n integer elements initialized to zero. Here, n may be read from input. values.size() returns the current size. values.push_back(x) appends an element and increases the size. An empty vector has no elements; values.empty() checks for this.

To read n numbers, create a vector of size n and access values[i] for i from 0 to n-1. For an unknown number of additions, start with std::vector<int> values; and call push_back. Do not confuse size with reserved capacity: elements exist only within size().

You can calculate a sum as a stream, but a vector is useful when you need the data again, in a different order, or after computing an overall property.

texts.cpp.while.theory:
while (condition) { ... } tests its condition before every iteration. It is useful when the repetition count is not known in advance. The body must change the state that controls continuation; otherwise the loop may run forever.

To process the digits of a positive n, take n%10 and remove the last digit using n/=10. The /= operator assigns the quotient back to the variable. Zero needs attention: while(n>0) does not execute for it. do { ... } while (condition); tests the condition after the body and executes at least once. This form requires a semicolon after while.

long long holds the larger integers used in these tasks; initial values and bounds must still be specified.

texts.cpp.windowlab.theory:
For a fixed-length window k, first sum the first k elements. On each rightward shift, add the entering a[right] and subtract the departing a[right-k]. Negative values are allowed: the length does not depend on the sum. For a maximum, do not initialize best=0 if every sum may be negative: use the first real window.

Variable length requires additional properties. For nonnegative elements, extending a window cannot decrease its sum, and removing from the left cannot increase it. If the sum exceeds limit, move the left boundary until valid. For a shortest window with sum at least target, record the length when the sum is sufficient and keep shrinking. Both pointers move only right, so the work is O(n), not O(n²).

To count all nonempty ranges with sum ≤limit, add right-left+1 after shrinking: every start between left and right is valid. Zeros matter: [0,0,0] has six ranges for limit=0. The variable-length tasks below use nonnegative input; the method must not be transferred to arbitrary negative values.
